newsitem.title: USA: FBI dismisses Navy missile theory in TWA crash.
newsitem.headline: FBI dismisses Navy missile theory in TWA crash.

text.p: Federal investigators on Wednesday dismissed claims that a U.S. Navy missile shot down TWA Flight 800 off Long Island, New York, last year.

"It's just not true," lead investigator James Kallstrom said on NBC's "Today Show." The assistant director of the FBI's New York office said investigators have reviewed every available radar picture of the accident and concluded there was no evidence of a missile being fired.

"There is no missile flying up at this plane on any of the radar tapes," he said. He also disputed claims by former presidential spokesman Pierre Salinger that there was a coverup of Navy involvement in the crash.
"As far as Salinger is concerned, almost all of what he says is wrong. All I can tell you is, it's wrong," Kallstrom said.

Salinger, who is also a former television correspondent, has scheduled a news conference for Thursday in Paris. Kallstrom said he was expected to announce he had an audiotape of Navy personnel expressing regret that they had shot down the TWA plane.
"I don't believe that it exists," Kallstrom said of the tape. "It's a cruel hoax. All of these people (with conspiracy theories) should get a life."
He was responding to reports of evidence that a missile caused the Boeing 747 to explode in midair off Long Island shortly after takeoff July 17, killing all 230 people on board.

Meanwhile, court sources said Wednesday the FBI had requested and obtained a copy of a videotape, allegedly a copy of a Federal Aviation Administration radar tape, that former United Airlines pilot Richard Russell claims shows an object streaking toward the plane seconds before it exploded after leaving Kennedy Airport on a flight to Paris.

Russell, of Daytona Beach, Florida, also posted an Internet message last year alleging a Navy missile was involved in the crash. He said in a message on his home telephone that he had been ordered to testify before a federal grand jury in New York Wednesday but authorities would not confirm this, noting that grand jury proceedings are kept secret.
Court sources said the FBI was not expected to speak to the retired pilot.

National Transportation Safety Board and FBI investigators have indicated that mechanical failure rather than a bomb or missile may have been responsible for the crash. Investigators know the centre fuel tank on the plane exploded but have not been able to explain why.
"I predict that Mr. Kallstrom will say they have the tape but it is a fraud. I assure you that it is the real thing," Russell said in his recorded message.
